title: Tensor+Pipeline Parallel scaling experiments and steady-state throughput harness
creator: Marina Patel
description: Define and implement a repeatable load-testing harness for measuring steady-state tokens/sec and tail latency (p95/p99) across tensor-parallel (TP) and pipeline-parallel (PP) distributed serving configurations. Goal: produce a stable benchmarking pipeline that can detect regressions (>=3% tokens/sec drop or >=10% p95 increase) against historical baselines and generate CI alerts. This ticket covers: test matrix design, harness implementation, CI job config, dashboard wiring, and initial runs for 7B/13B/70B families with quantized vs fp16 variants.
test_matrix: models: rwi-7b, rwi-13b, rwi-70b (representative open variants)
benchmarking_rules: Use deterministic synthetic prompts with seeded RNG for reproducibility
Warmup phase: 2 minutes (discard metrics) to populate KV cache and JIT kernels
Steady-state measurement: 10 minute window unless noted otherwise
Report tokens/sec as the total emitted tokens divided by steady-state seconds
Report latency percentiles (p50,p95,p99) measured per request end-to-end
Exclude outliers beyond 3 sigma for tokens/sec aggregation but keep tail latencies for p99 analysis
Capture GPU utilization, PCIe traffic, alltoall bandwidth, and memory fragmentation at 10s resolution
Run each cell in the matrix 3 times and report median; store raw traces for statistical tests
regression_detection: Baseline: rolling 30-day median for each (model,tp,pp,seq,microbatch,quant) tuple
Trigger: tokens/sec drop >= 3% with p-value < 0.05 using Mann-Whitney U on paired runs
Tail alert: p95 increase >= 10% and absolute p95 > 200ms for low-latency targets
Noise floor estimation: compute coefficient of variation across runs; require CV < 4% for a tuple to be considered stable
Automated rollback / canary gating: hook into rollout pipeline to block runtime upgrades when regression detected
implementation_notes: Harness implemented as a Kubernetes job set (bench-runner) that orchestrates model workers and a traffic generator pod
Traffic generator supports both steady open-loop token emission and replay of production traces (to be used in Phase 2)
Use NCCL for TP allreduce/alltoall; measure alternative Gloo runs for environments where NCCL isn't available
Add a lightweight sidecar that streams perf counters to Prometheus, tag runs with git SHA and docker image
Store results as NDJSON artifacts in S3 (one file per run) and push summary to BenchDB for historical baselines
results_summary: Initial runs (2026-02-28): rwi-13b tp=4 pp=2 microbatch=4 seq=512 => median tokens/sec=128k, p95=210ms
rwi-70b tp=8 pp=4 microbatch=1 seq=2048 => median tokens/sec=48k, p95=720ms (high variance observed)
Int8-ptq gave 18%-25% tokens/sec improvement for rwi-13b at same latency budget; memory fragmentation increased for pp>2
Observed an 8% tokens/sec regression in one CI run correlated with NCCL version mismatch — created ENG-9610 to track NCCL pinning
Measured noise floor for canonical tuples around 2.5% CV, meets stability requirement for most 7B/13B runs but not for 70B at long seq lengths
open_questions: Should we canonicalize on a single backend (NCCL) for CI or run both NCCL+Gloo to catch environment-specific regressions?
What is the correct steady-state window for 70B with long seqs where cache warmup is significant? Increase to 20 minutes?
Do we gate releases on tokens/sec-only or include p95/p99 thresholds in the canary policy?
next_steps: Stabilize CI: add retry-run, increase run count to 5 for high-variance cells (assigned Diego)
Add cost-normalized metrics (tokens/sec per GPU-hour) for Dedicated capacity planning (assigned Marina)
Implement baseline updater job that computes rolling medians and submits derived alerts to PagerDuty (ENG-9612)
Add a replay mode using sampled production traces (follow-on ticket PM-412)
